name: services-page
title: Services page
description: A calm page for someone who sells their time (a coach, consultant, tutor or freelancer): a one-line promise with a booking button, services with prices, how it works, what clients say, questions, about you, workshops and how to reach you.

images.purpose: beside the headline on the home page: the person at work, or their space; without it the headline sits beside a small card with their email, phone and availability
images.alt_hint: who and what it shows, e.g. Ada at her desk going through a client's receipts
images.prompt: a real, well-lit photo of {subject} at work or welcoming a client, looking toward the camera, room around them on the left and right

images.purpose: the mark beside the name in the header (40 px, rounded corners) and the browser icon; must still read at 32 px
images.alt_hint: e.g. A leaf over an open ledger
images.prompt: a simple flat emblem for {subject}, one shape, in the accent colour on the page's background colour, no words

images.purpose: the picture when a link is shared; empty uses the hero
images.alt_hint: what it shows, then the name and promise if they are written in it
images.prompt: the hero photo cropped wide, with room on one side for the name and the one-line promise

images.purpose: a photo across the top of a service card (a session in progress, the finished work); leave every card in a group without one or give each one
images.prompt: a real photo of {subject} giving this service

images.purpose: a photo at the top of a workshop's or post's own page
images.prompt: a real photo from the workshop or its room

content.purpose: the promise in one line, the big headline (e.g. Calm, practical help with your books)
under the headline: who it is for and the problem you solve, two or three sentences
the main button under the headline (with cta_link): where people book, e.g. Book a free call, linking out to the booking page; cta2_label and cta2_link make a second, e.g. See prices -> #g-services

everything in boxes, sorted into groups (card.group), each group its own section headed by its group name, in the cards' sort order. How a group looks follows what its cards carry: with a price it is the services (name, description = what you get, period = how long, price, link = book this); with a subtitle and no price it is testimonials (description = the quote, name = who said it, subtitle = their role or town; ask permission for every name); with a period and no price it is numbered steps (How it works: name, description, period = the step's label or length, e.g. First week); with none of those it is questions and answers (name = the question, description = the answer)
the heading of cards that have no group; the menu item for the cards (cards_nav overrides it)
about you (about_title is its heading): short credentials; the first paragraph prints larger

a list stream of entries with an event (date, place, RSVP link) shows as upcoming workshops or sessions, then earlier ones; a stream without events lists its posts; a feature stream shows its newest post in full

email and phone show in the card beside the headline and in the Contact section at the end; the address (or just a town for the area you serve) and social links show there too. The Contact menu item and section appear when there is any

when you take calls or sessions: the weekly table and whether you are available now (also in the card beside the headline), holidays in the next 60 days, and a note (e.g. Replies within one working day)
big link buttons at the top of the Contact section, the first one filled: e.g. Book a free 20-minute call, Send me your paperwork; note is the small line under each
a banner across the top of every page, e.g. Taking new clients from January
the footer line, e.g. the business name and the area served

art.ask: Ask for one friendly, well-lit photo of them working or welcoming a client. A face builds trust.
art.style: Photographs; no stock photos of handshakes. Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
steps: Get the photos from your person: one of them at work for the hero, and any of real sessions or finished work for the service cards.
Check each one: sharp, well lit, the right shape (crop to the slot's size), nobody in it who hasn't agreed to be there.
Write alt text for each: who is in it and what they are doing.
Upload each one (an https link in its field, or photo_upload_link), then call theme_needs: every slot you used should say filled.
Ask for permission for every named testimonial before it goes on the page.
Use real photos for real things; never make up pictures of real places, people or food. Illustrated art only for a mark or emblem, in the palette's accent colour.
